column1: # The four genomes of the tiny test database. Pinned by VERSIONED accession:
# an unversioned accession tracks the latest revision and would silently change
# the database, and with it every committed baseline.
# One genome per threshold class, so that each cov_thresh_*/minimizer_thresh_*
# branch in filter_kraken_reports.py is exercised by a real sample.
# seq_taxid is what the FASTA header is tagged with. For three of the four it is
# the STRAIN taxid, which Kraken2 reports one level below species (rank code S1);
# phiX174 is tagged at species level (S). That mix is deliberate — it exercises
# both arms of the "lowest rank for this species" logic in
# filter_kraken_reports.py, which treats an S line followed by S1 differently
# from an S line standing alone.
# The fifth genome is tagged at GENUS level on purpose, and is not one of the
# four threshold classes. Without it, every row of library/species_genome_size.txt
# resolves to a species, pandas types the species_level_taxa column as int64, and
# scale_bracken.py dies on
#   ValueError: You are trying to merge on object and int64 columns
# because it casts the Bracken side to str. The real Phanta database never hits
# this: it holds many genomes classified no further than genus, for which
# calculate_genome_size.py writes the literal 'error - taxid above species',
# which forces the column to object and makes the merge string-to-string. A
# tiny database with no such genome is unrepresentative, and fails in a way the
# real one does not. This is not a pandas-version issue — pandas 1.5.3 raises
# the same error.
# sha256 is of the raw FASTA as fetched from NCBI, before header rewriting.
